title: Tourism BC & Destination BC
subtitle: Brands, websites and visitor experiences
description: Follow British Columbia’s tourism identity across logos, travel websites, training programs and publications. A 2013 asset-transfer inventory ties the family together; dated publications add the visual evidence.
scopeNote: The 2013 inventory documents assets and names listed for transfer. It is not a register of current ownership, active websites or logo-adoption dates. Tourism BC, the Province’s tourism operation and Destination BC retain separate corporate histories.

digitalRecords.title: HelloBC and SupernaturalBC.com
digitalRecords.description: The consumer travel network links the tourism identity to websites, trip ideas and destination listings. The 2013 schedule names a ten-market global web platform; a separate 2025 announcement records the move to SupernaturalBC.com.

sourceRefs.locator: Printed page 12, Squamish Visitor Centre HelloBC listing

links.label: SupernaturalBC.com
links.note: Consumer site named in Destination BC’s launch announcement.

digitalRecords.dateNote: 1 April 2009 is the global platform’s in-service date in the asset schedule, not the first launch of every HelloBC website. The later site launched 10 September 2025.
digitalRecords.internationalNote: These are the ten markets printed in Appendix 8. Appendix 5’s country-address variants do not establish which domain served each platform, or that every listed address hosted a separate website.

digitalRecords.title: SuperHost and WorldHost
digitalRecords.description: Tourism service training connects the SuperHost and WorldHost names, their illustrated marks, international adaptations and a dedicated training website. The order lists training domains and WorldHost Training Services as a program area.
digitalRecords.dateNote: A registration, transferred domain or later website reproduction does not establish the program’s creation or current operation.

digitalRecords.title: Near Me BC
digitalRecords.description: An early iPhone visitor application used location and mapping to help users find nearby tourism businesses. The 2010 service plan describes more than 4,000 HelloBC listings and GPS/Google Maps features; the 2013 inventory lists two related domains.
digitalRecords.dateNote: Documented as launched by the minister’s message dated 18 February 2010. The precise launch date and an original app interface are not established here.

digitalRecords.title: BC Escapes
digitalRecords.description: A consumer campaign documented from late February 2003. ESCAPES, BC ESCAPES and BRITISH COLUMBIA ESCAPES are listed as word marks, alongside a group of related domains. A named campaign is documented even while its original website interface remains to be recovered.
digitalRecords.dateNote: Late February 2003 dates the documented campaign, not every domain or graphical treatment.

digitalRecords.title: British Columbia Magazine
digitalRecords.description: The transfer schedule connects the magazine’s illustrated identity to publishing, subscriptions and several web addresses. Its design belongs with the tourism collection, while the magazine and its websites retain their own history.
digitalRecords.dateNote: The 2013 transfer is a dated ownership/program record. It does not date the magazine’s foundation or establish today’s publisher or website ownership.

digitalRecords.title: Share Your B.C.
digitalRecords.description: A public photography campaign linked British Columbia Magazine and BC Parks. The 2011 announcement uses shareyourbc.ca, while the 2013 transfer inventory lists shareyourbc.com; both spellings are retained as separate observations.

historicalAddresses.note: Address in the 2011 announcement; not a replacement for the .com entry in Appendix 5.

digitalRecords.dateNote: The contest is documented for 15 March–30 September 2011. No current operation is asserted.

digitalRecords.title: Tourism BC online
digitalRecords.description: The corporate and industry-facing addresses sit beside the consumer websites. The order’s supplier terms name TourismBC.net, while Appendix 8 records tourism product-management and DMS systems with their own in-service dates.

sourceRefs.locator: Industry Marketing Programs terms and conditions
Appendix 8: Tourism Product Management and DMS

digitalRecords.dateNote: Tourism BC’s corporation ended in 2010; the Province continued tourism functions before the 2013 transfer. Website and brand activity are not evidence of uninterrupted corporate existence.

digitalRecords.title: Destination BC online
digitalRecords.description: Destination BC’s corporate website and its portfolio of proposed or registered geographic variants belong beside its separate consumer travel brand. The 2013 inventory is a source for those addresses, not evidence that each had a public website.

links.label: Destination BC
links.note: Corporate site; distinct from the consumer travel site.

digitalRecords.dateNote: The corporation was established on 2 November 2012 and began operations on 1 April 2013. Neither date is automatically a domain registration or website launch date.

digitalRecords.title: Canada’s West and Canada’s West Marketplace

timeline.title: Tourism BC’s statutory beginning
timeline.description: The Tourism British Columbia Act was given retroactive effect from this date. The later assent date is a separate legislative event.

timeline.title: BC Escapes campaign
timeline.description: The 2004 service plan reports a campaign launched in late February 2003.

timeline.title: A published visual system
timeline.description: The December 2005 graphic standards document the corporate, consumer and international logo system. The edition dates these specimens, not every design’s adoption.

timeline.title: Tourism product and program systems
timeline.description: Appendix 8 gives this in-service date for Tourism Product Management and DMS Program Management.

timeline.title: A network of ten market websites
timeline.description: The consumer web platform, DMS Integration and DMS Inntopia are recorded as in service on this date. It does not establish the first launch of all related domains.

timeline.title: Near Me BC is documented
timeline.description: The minister’s message describes a launched iPhone visitor app; an exact launch day is not established.

timeline.title: Tourism BC’s work returns to government
timeline.description: The Tourism BC corporation was dissolved and its assets and obligations vested in government. Tourism functions continued within the Province before the later transfer to Destination BC.

timeline.title: Share Your BC contest
timeline.description: BC Parks’ report describes the British Columbia Magazine / BC Parks contest running to 30 September 2011.

timeline.title: 100 BC Moments campaign
timeline.description: The announcement connects a campaign microsite and HelloBC. The name later appears among the official marks in the transfer schedule.

timeline.title: Destination BC is established
timeline.description: The later corporation was established under the Business Corporations Act. Its operational start follows in April 2013.

timeline.title: An inventory of the tourism estate
timeline.description: Ministerial Order 68/2013 authorizes transfer under an agreement covering marks, domains, websites, copyright and program materials. The document provides a dated snapshot of that portfolio.

timeline.title: Operations and the asset-transfer agreement
timeline.description: Destination BC began operations on this date. The agreement names it as the completion date unless the parties agree otherwise, transferring assets from the Province rather than continuing the old Tourism BC corporation.
timeline.dateRole: operational start and agreement completion date

timeline.title: SupernaturalBC.com launches
timeline.description: Destination BC’s October announcement dates the new consumer website’s launch to 10 September and publishes an image of the interface.

publications.title: Tourism BC graphic standards, December 2005
publications.description: The December 2005 manual documents logo arrangements, minimum sizes and colour treatments. The publication has been located, and native vector specimens from it are included in this collection.

publications.title: Approved Accommodation Guide
publications.description: The supplier terms and a publishing contract name the Approved Accommodation Guide. Complete issues, including covers and interior listings, are still sought for this collection.

publications.title: British Columbia Insider’s Guide
publications.description: The industry marketing terms name British Columbia Insider’s Guide alongside the accommodation guide. Complete issues are still sought for this collection.

publications.title: British Columbia Magazine issues
publications.description: The transfer schedule and 2013 service plan document the magazine publishing program. The collection holds masthead specimens; complete issues and dated cover examples are still sought.

publications.title: HelloBC brochures and maps
publications.description: Appendix 8 lists website copy, maps and PDFs, and the domain schedule includes brochures.hellobc.com. Individual brochures and maps with documented publication dates and publishers are still sought.

publications.title: SuperHost / WorldHost training materials
publications.description: The program inventory documents training curricula, workshops and industry programs. Manuals, certificates and examples of the training identities in use are still sought.

publications.title: Photographs, films and campaign artwork
publications.description: The transfer includes photographic, video, illustration and brand-guideline material. Individual photograph, film and campaign-artwork files from these holdings are still sought.
